data.final_week_advice: Prioritize mastering energy conservation and free-body diagrams, as these are foundational for the exam. Use the live class in Week 2 to solidify your understanding of work and energy, then apply these concepts to complex problems in subsequent weeks. Keep a consistent study schedule and review weak areas regularly to build confidence before the exam.
data.summary: This 5-week plan focuses on strengthening Unit 3 (Work, Energy, and Power) early, leveraging the live class in Week 2. It balances new material with regular review and timed practice, ensuring all units are covered while prioritizing weak areas. The final week is dedicated to mixed review and exam preparation.

tasks: Complete 20 multiple-choice questions on 1D and 2D kinematics, marking errors for review
Draw and analyze 5 free-body diagrams for objects in equilibrium and motion
Solve 10 problems applying Newton's Second Law to systems with friction

weeks.focus: Deepen understanding of work, energy, and power
tasks: Attend live class on work and energy conservation
Solve 15 problems on kinetic and potential energy transformations
Calculate power in 5 real-world scenarios, explaining each step
Analyze 5 rotational systems, calculating torque and angular acceleration
Solve 8 problems connecting linear and rotational motion
Graph and analyze 5 SHM scenarios, identifying period and amplitude
Solve 10 fluid pressure and flow rate problems
Review energy conservation in oscillating systems with 5 practice questions
Complete a full 3-hour timed practice exam, reviewing all units
Redo 10 missed questions from the practice exam, focusing on weak areas
Summarize key formulas and concepts for each unit in a one-page cheat sheet
